subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these six AI-safety event names and fields as a stable core and Plugin SDK contract, with safety emission restricted to a core-internal function plus the manifest-authorized plugin API?
rationale: The patch creates a durable public taxonomy and security-sensitive trust boundary; code review can identify defects but cannot choose the permanent product vocabulary, privacy/cardinality contract, or whether this belongs in stable core SDK surface.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded taxonomy
options.body: Approve the six-event core contract after adding per-event schema versions, removing AI-safety payloads from the public trusted emitter, and proving the authorized plugin path.

options.title: Keep it internal and experimental
options.body: Land no public SDK exports yet; first instrument a smaller internal-only taxonomy and promote it after operator and exporter experience validates the fields.

options.title: Pause the feature series
options.body: Close or defer the linked implementation PRs until a maintainer-owned observability design defines the taxonomy and trust model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded taxonomy
recommendation.body: Approve the six-event core contract after adding per-event schema versions, removing AI-safety payloads from the public trusted emitter, and proving the authorized plugin path.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly relevant current-main history is the diagnostics trusted-provenance and internal-subscription hardening work.
